title: Global Head of Data Science, Analytics & AI
description:
Job Description:
The Global Head of Data Science, Analytics & AI for Mars Snacking is a pivotal senior leadership role, that will be joining at a time of transformation for the Segment, following the recent acquisition of Kellanova, We are seeking a visionary leader to shape and execute our segment's Analytics & AI strategy. Reporting to the SVP Chief Data & Analytics Officer, and a member of the CDAO leadership team, you will be instrumental in powering our strategic priorities delivering leading digital products and capabilities, developing the governance & frameworks for how we lead in this space, and building a best-in-class team.
Mars Snacking is at the start of a hugely exciting journey, integrating two incredibly successful organizations with exciting and category leading brands. This position requires a leader who can innovate, excite, and help shape our future; ensuring data, analytics, and AI are core enablers of our growth across a newly expanded portfolio. As a key member of the CDAO leadership team, you will be responsible for co-creating a vision and strategy that will help steer the organisation through complexity and change, keeping a sharp focus on value creation and a winning culture.
What are we looking for?
Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or PhD in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, or a related discipline preferred.
12+ years of experience in the data and analytics space with at least 5 years in a senior leadership capacity managing large, technical teams.
Proven experience in Product Management, specifically within the AI, Data Science, and Machine Learning domains.
Strong stakeholder relationship management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate with senior leaders across a large enterprise.
Deep technical knowledge in Machine Learning, Data Science, and Computational Science.
Demonstrated experience in AI strategy development and successful implementation.
Experience managing vendor and partner relationships to drive innovation and execution.
A strong understanding of User Experience (UX) principles in the context of AI and analytics products.
Solid experience in business case development and feasibility assessment for technical projects.
Ideally experience in a CPG or Retail environment.
Experience working across leading technology platforms including GCP Gemini, Databricks, Azure, etc.
What will be your key responsibilities?
AI Strategy & Vision : Lead the development and application of the strategic vision for data science, analytics, and AI for the Snacking segment, partnering with functional, regional, and divisional leaders to deliver innovative and scalable solutions.
Team Leadership : Build, engage, and develop a high-performing global team of Data Science, Analytics & AI associates, establishing clear ways of working and accountabilities.
Stakeholder Management / Business Partnership : Be the strategic partner of choice for the segment regions, functions & divisions by deeply understanding the business needs, identifying opportunities for scale and providing innovative solutions and recommendations.
Deliver Business Value : Support the regions, functions and divisions on the delivery of our integration priorities with purpose and pace.
Operational Excellence O: Ensure operational excellence and accelerate quality growth through the creation of advanced analytics and AI capabilities, such as SRM (Strategic Revenue Management) and Perfect Store, Perfect Service agentic tools.
Capability & Governance : Establish a clear vision, strategy, and framework to ensure a consistent, scalable, and high-quality approach to Analytics & AI, ensuring value realization and adherence to governance and ethical practices.
Elevate AI Literacy : Act as an accelerator and champion for AI maturity growth across the segment, elevating capabilities and sponsoring valuable experimentation and scale.
Technology & Architecture : Contribute to the architectural direction for analytics technology solutions and partner with internal IT and external partners to maximize the value derived from our technology platforms.
Innovation & Research : Lead the research and evaluation of emerging skills, models, and market trends, bringing forward recommendations and solutions to achieve our long-term vision.
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

Job Description:
Job Summary/Purpose: This Senior Associate Scientist role plays an important role in supporting, planning, and executing laboratory projects to support regional and global R&D teams. This role will be responsible for conducting physical and chemical analyses on raw materials and finished products with emphasis on front end innovation, ingredient characterization, site investigations, and product performance/competitiveness. The primary scope of this role is to execute analytical testing and communicate scientific insights, and conduct technical consultations in support of PNNA and Global R&D stakeholders. The Sr Associate Scientist will collaborate with large cross functional teams within the R&D function to achieve strategic objectives.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Experience : 2-4 years’ experience in a laboratory setting with functional/physical characterization of raw materials, in-process products, protein knowledge, or finished goods in food or related industries (advanced education may partially substitute for required experience).
Proven laboratory methodology capabilities and/or familiarity with a wide range of food analysis methodologies, including but not limited to flavor/aroma characterization (GC-MS, LC-MS, GC-O), material characterization (DSC, TGA, FT-IR, etc.), rheology/flowability, and product characterization (texture, color, in-vitro digestibility)
Excellent practical laboratory skills, including the ability to troubleshoot and maintain complex analytical instrumentation.
Demonstrated ability to follow established laboratory safety procedures, maintain accurate records, and clearly and accurately read, write, and interpret data.
Demonstrated and proven written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred Experience: 4 - 6 years’ experience with functional/physical characterization of raw materials, in-process products, or finished goods in food or related industries (advanced education may partially substitute for required experience).
Familiarity with shelf-life testing protocols a plus
What will be your key responsibilities?
Perform analytics on raw ingredients and finished products to determine physical and chemical characteristics and behaviors. The methods that this Sr Associate Scientist would perform may include LC-MS, GC-MS, Aroma Profiling, UV-Vis spectroscopy, Flowability and Rheology methodology, and material characterization tools such as Optical Particle Distribution, Differential Scanning Calorimetry, TGA, DVS, Texture, and Organoleptic/Sensory observations etc.
Record or compile test results or prepare graphs, charts, or reports using electronic lab notebook (ELN) and clearly present experimental results to R&D stakeholders.
Consulting with R&D scientists, engineers, and technical partners and delivering on strategic project requests. This role will frequently interface with other R&D associates to present findings, design test protocols, report data, clarify results, contribute to experimental designs, and recommend future direction for broader R&D.
Lead or support the development, validation, and implementation of new analytical methods to address emerging technical and business needs.

title: Technologist, Quality & Food Safety
description:
Job Description:
The Technologist, Quality & Food Safety (Q&FS) is responsible for ensuring all relevant Q&FS standards are implemented and continuously improved to assure quality and food safety at the local site, protecting the consumer and our brands. Operating at the intersection of systematic compliance and factory floor execution, this role provides the hands-on technical expertise needed to identify, mitigate, and control biological, chemical, and physical hazards before they impact our products or consumers.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in food science, Microbiology, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, a closely related scientific discipline or equivalent
2+ years in a food or related manufacturing facility, with hands-on experience in HACCP, food safety management systems, and internal auditing.
Strong ability to lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and write clear, audit-ready technical procedures.
Strong technical courage to confidently halt production or hold inventory, alongside excellent communication skills to coach floor operators.
Ability to stand and walk the manufacturing floor for prolonged periods of time, working safely around high-speed machinery in hot, dusty, or noisy plant environments.
10% travel
Preferred Qualifications
Active HACCP, HARPC, or PCQI (Preventive Controls Qualified Individual) certification
FSSC 22000 internal auditor certification
High proficiency in Microsoft Office; direct experience with SAP
What will be your key responsibilities?
Standards & Regulatory Alignment : Ensure all site processes and procedures strictly comply with corporate Mars Quality and Food Safety Standards, Business Unit directives, and regulatory agency regulations.
HACCP & Risk Management:  Serve as a core Food Safety Representative for the site HACCP Team and Food Safety Team, leading and supporting risk assessments for all facility changes (CAB, new products/packaging/processes) and validating Critical Control Points (CCPs).
Incident & Hold Management:  Manage the site product hold-and-release programs within SAP, NCMGT, and Nexus. Ensuring proper isolation, disposition, and destruction of non-conforming materials and products.
Audit & CAPA Leadership:  Supports site internal audits and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) programs to drive continuous system improvements.
Incident Response & RCA:  Serve as a PRIMP (Product Related Incident Management Process) owner, leading structured root-cause analysis (RCA) sessions and recommending corrective actions.
Continuous Improvement:  Works to identify defects and trends in site processes.  Develop and/or lead improvement projects in alignment with the Site Q&FS Manager.
Capability & Training:  Develop and deliver interactive food safety and GMP training modules to build technical capability and a strong quality culture among site associates.
Finished Product Release:  Execute the final release of finished products, ensuring all quality and food safety specifications have been met.
Other Duties: assigned by the Site Quality and Food Safety Manager
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
Best-in-class learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:
The Manager, Return to Vendor (RTV) is a key individual contributor within the Sourcing organization responsible for overseeing the end-to-end RTV process across the company's retail and e-commerce supply chain. This role serves as the primary point of contact for vendor return negotiations, disputes, and recovery, ensuring that defective, excess, and non-conforming merchandise is resolved efficiently and that the company maximizes recovery value. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, a skilled negotiator, and comfortable operating cross-functionally with Merchandising, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Vendor partners.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
RTV Program Ownership
Own and manage the full RTV lifecycle — from claim initiation through resolution, credit receipt, or physical return logistics.
Establish and maintain a centralized RTV tracking system; monitor open claims, aging balances, and recovery rates.
Develop and enforce RTV policies, standard operating procedures, and escalation protocols.
Partner with Buying and Planning teams to identify and prioritize RTV candidates across categories.
Vendor Negotiation & Relationship Management
Lead direct negotiations with vendor partners to secure credits, replacements, or return authorizations in alignment with contractual terms.
Build and maintain productive vendor relationships while assertively advocating for the company's financial interests.
Review and interpret vendor contracts and purchase order terms related to returns, defects, and chargebacks.
Identify recurring quality or compliance issues with vendors and escalate to the Sourcing Director for strategic action.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with the Logistics and Warehouse teams to coordinate physical return shipments, disposition of goods, and inbound/outbound documentation.
Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable to ensure timely posting of vendor credits and accurate reconciliation of RTV balances.
Work with the Quality Assurance team to document and report on product defect trends to inform future sourcing decisions.
Support Buying teams during vendor onboarding to ensure RTV terms and expectations are clearly defined.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement
Produce regular reporting on RTV volume, recovery rate, aging claims, and open liabilities for senior leadership review.
Identify process gaps and implement improvements to reduce cycle time, increase recovery, and minimize dispute resolution time.
Benchmark RTV performance against industry standards and recommend best practices.
REQUIREMENTS:
5+ years of experience in sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or supply chain — with direct RTV, chargeback, or vendor compliance exposure.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with vendor partners, including knowledge of contract terms, credit processes, and dispute resolution.

This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position is tailored for an experienced, high-level Senior Field Service Technician who will serve as a technical expert and leader in supporting complex vehicle repairs and field operations. The role requires an adaptable, team-oriented leader capable of driving continuous improvement, mentoring junior team members, and tackling complex diagnostic challenges in a fast-paced environment. While based primarily at a service center, this role may involve operating remotely, traveling to remote locations, or working at production plants to provide advanced field support as business needs demand. Candidates will be evaluated against a comprehensive spectrum of advanced technical skills and leadership capabilities. Responsibilities Advanced Diagnostics & Complex Repairs: Perform bumper-to-bumper diagnostics, complex repairs, installations, and inspections on vehicles both inside service centers and in field settings (customer sites, mobile routes, or remote locations). Technical Support & Remote Troubleshooting: Provide high-level diagnostic guidance to field service teams and perform remote diagnostics or repairs for issues that can be safely addressed without local vehicle access by evaluating logged vehicle data and technical schematics. Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and train junior technicians and internal partners; foster cross-functional collaboration and lead shop-floor technical problem-solving. Advanced Tools & Methodologies: Utilize specialized diagnostic tools (e.g., PICO-Scope, PCAN, Kavaser Memorator, breakout boxes) to resolve complex electrical, high-voltage, and network faults. Quality & Process Standardization: Conduct thorough road tests to verify repair quality, champion continuous improvement processes, and drive high standards across repair workflows. Parts Operations & Systems: Oversee complex parts operations—including ordering, receiving, inventory management, and billing—to ensure quality and operational efficiency. Documentation & Technical Feedback: Produce high-quality documentation in service support and engineering systems; provide root-cause analysis and actionable feedback to field service engineers and leadership. Customer & Cross-Functional Engagement: Interact professionally with customers, suppliers, and internal teams during escalation resolutions or mobile outreach events. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school or vocational program preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). State mechanic certifications where required by jurisdiction (e.g., Michigan certifications in front end, suspension, steering, brakes, electrical, and HVAC). Experience & Leadership: 5 to 8+ years of automotive repair experience preferred, with extensive experience in bumper-to-bumper diagnostics. 3 to 8+ years of hands-on experience working on vehicle High Voltage (HV) systems and HV diagnostic work. Experience in leadership or supervisory roles (e.g., Shop Foreman, Team Lead, or Technical Mentor) preferred. Demonstrated background in continuous improvement, process standardization, and escalation management. Spectrum of Advanced Technical Skills: High Voltage (HV) & Power Electronics: Deep understanding of high-voltage architecture, High-Voltage Interlock Loops (HVIL), charging isolation, and safety power-down protocols using appropriate PPE. Capable of diagnosing complex HV faults and isolation issues. Low Voltage & Network Electronics: Advanced knowledge of automotive electronics, CAN and LIN bus network communication, reading/leveraging electrical schematics, and performing precise wiring harness repairs. Chassis, Drivability & Dynamic Systems: Mastery in chassis service (alignments, braking systems) and advanced diagnosis of vehicle dynamics (ABS, traction control, power steering, and Noise, Vibration, and Harshness / NVH concerns). Thermal & HVAC Systems: Comprehensive knowledge of HVAC systems, coolant drain/fill operations, A/C machine usage, 609 refrigerant certification, and diagnosing complex thermal management issues. ADAS & Body/Glass Integration: Proficiency in calibrating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and replacing/adjusting sensors, body panels, and glass to precise manufacturer tolerances. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs. description:

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and argue for the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. At the Senior level, you are a force multiplier for your team. Through thoughtful designs, rigorous reviews, hands-on mentorship, and sound technical judgment, you help other engineers deliver better work. You lead by example, strengthen engineering practices, and connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. You bring clarity to ambiguous problems, act with intellectual honesty and urgency, and deliver high-quality solutions iteratively.
What you bring
8+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , You have delivered reliable firmware where memory, processing power, energy and timing are all scarce, and you know how to measure, optimize and make deliberate trade-offs between them.
You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.
Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

title: CV/ML Camera Test Engineer
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring a hands-on CV/ML camera test engineer to measure how camera and optics choices affect the performance of our AI models. Working with our Optics & Camera Engineering Lead, this individual will turn experiment plans into lab and field setups, run the campaigns, push the data through our CV/ML models and report what changed and why. The work is scientific at its core: reason from first principles about optics, sensor physics and illumination, form a hypothesis, design a controlled experiment to test it, and let the data decide. This individual will collaborate with camera, CV/ML, software, hardware and field teams to put data behind every camera decision.

Responsibilities:

 - Form testable hypotheses from first principles (optics, sensor physics, radiometry and illumination), and design controlled experiments with defined variables, controls, sample sizes and success criteria before collecting data.

 - Execute experiments comparing sensors, lenses, ISP settings, IR illumination, focus and window conditions, and measure their effect on detection, recognition and LPR performance at range.

 - Build and maintain lab and outdoor test setups, including targets at known distances, controlled lighting and low-light scenes, IR illumination and chamber runs across temperature.

 - Run field data-collection campaigns across sites, times of day, lighting and weather, keeping conditions, metadata and ground truth consistent.

 - Run captured video through existing CV/ML models and evaluation tools, and compute model metrics alongside image-quality measurements (MTF, SNR, distortion, pixels on target).

 - Script captures, camera settings, data pipelines and analysis in Python and shell on embedded Linux devices so every run is reproducible.

 - Isolate the cause of performance changes across optics, sensor, ISP, illumination and environment, using statistical analysis rather than anecdote, and write clear reports that state confidence, limitations and recommendations.

 - Support camera validation (focus stability, thermal, condensation, IR range) through EVT, DVT and PVT.



Qualifications:

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and being scrappy.

 - Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.

 - 2+ years of experience in hardware test, validation or experimental work.

 - Strong Linux command line proficiency (required), including SSH, logs, file and process management and shell scripting on embedded devices.

 - Proficient in Python for scripting, data processing and analysis.

 - A scientific, first-principles mindset: you reason from the physics to predict results, design controlled experiments to test those predictions, and change your mind when the data says so.

 - Hands-on with test setups and lab equipment, and comfortable doing outdoor field work, including at night and in bad weather.

 - Strong grounding in statistics and experimental design, including hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, variance, sample sizing and trends across campaigns.

 - Exceptional organization and communication skills (both written and oral).

 - No CV/ML background required. You'll use our existing models and evaluation tools and learn the rest on the job.



Nice to Have

 - Experience with cameras, image sensors, lenses or image-quality testing (MTF, SNR, low light, IR).

 - Exposure to computer vision tools (OpenCV) or ML evaluation metrics such as precision and recall.

 - Experience with video tooling such as FFmpeg, GStreamer or V4L2.

 - Experience with thermal chambers, reliability or production test.

 - Background in physics, optics or a research lab environment.


Tool Proficiency

 - Linux command line and shell scripting (required).

 - Python with NumPy, pandas and plotting libraries.

 - Git for scripts and test procedures.

 - Imatest or equivalent image-quality tools (preferred).

title: Optics & Camera Engineering Lead
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring an Optics & Camera Engineering Lead to own camera performance across our product portfolio. This individual will own the imaging stack end to end: sensor and lens selection, optical requirements tied to CV/ML and customer outcomes, vendor and JDM programs, test campaigns and results analysis, and high volume production. This individual will collaborate with systems, software, CV/ML, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain and test teams to deliver performant, scalable and validated camera + optical systems to the field.

The role spans the full stack. One day you'll be benchmarking sensors and lenses for a new product. Next, you'll work with our CV/ML team to translate detection, recognition and LPR performance at range into pixel density, MTF and low-light targets, or review athermal lens designs, define a slant-edge MTF test across temperature, or analyze a wiper endurance run. You'll work with systems, software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing and supply chain, and lead technical engagements with tier-one optics and sensor suppliers.



Responsibilities:

Select sensors and lenses

 - Evaluate and select image sensors for each product, comparing low-light performance (SNR1s, QE at 850/940 nm), pixel size, resolution, frame rate, HDR, supply life and cost.

 - Select off-the-shelf lenses or specify custom designs matched to each sensor: FOV, F-number, MTF across the field, NIR correction, distortion, relative illumination and athermal behavior.

 - Evaluate and select the ISP architecture (on-sensor, companion ASIC/FPGA or SoC ISP), weighing image quality, latency, power, cost and supply, and drive ISP tuning and pipeline development for day and NIR night modes.

 - Benchmark sensor and lens candidates side by side in the lab and the field, and keep a qualified roster of sensors, lenses and IR-cut filters ready for new programs.

Connect customer value to optical requirements

 - Translate customer use cases and CV/ML performance into camera requirements using pixel-density frameworks such as IEC 62676-4 DORI.

 - Run coverage and range trade studies across sensor resolution, FOV, mounting height, pixel density, IR range, inference load, power and cost.

 - Define MTF, aperture, distortion, relative illumination, stray light and NIR focus targets, and tie them to measured model precision and recall at distance.

 - Design and run real-world field test campaigns across sites, lighting and weather, and use the resulting model and image-quality data to close the loop from camera change to quantified customer impact and drive design decisions.

Own optical and camera system design

 - Own optical performance specifications for fixed, multi-camera, panoramic and PTZ products.

 - Integrate the selected sensor, lens, IR-cut filter and mount into a camera system that meets spec across every operating condition.

 - Drive athermal design so focus and MTF hold across a wide operating range under solar loading, accounting for IR-cut filters, lens mounts, flange CTE, humidity and pressure.

 - Specify NIR illumination (LED and laser) matched to lens FOV, including frame-synced strobing, IEC 60825-1 eye safety, thermal limits and internal-reflection control.

 - Guide window, coating, heater, wiper and sun-shade design so optical performance survives years of outdoor service.

 - Use optical simulation to evaluate concepts quickly and review supplier prescriptions with confidence.

Lead vendor and JDM programs

 - Own the technical content of RFPs for camera modules and complete camera systems, and evaluate proposals on performance, cost, schedule and risk.

 - Lead technical work with optics suppliers and ODM/JDM partners on off-the-shelf selection, custom lens design, active alignment and production test.

 - Hold partners to design reviews and gate criteria from design through EVT, DVT and PVT.

Build test capability and run campaigns

 - Grow Specter's optical lab: collimators, slant-edge MTF, focus through temperature, flare and stray light, low-light SNR, IR range and FOV/distortion measurement.

 - Design and qualify optical test equipment for development, reliability and manufacturing, with documented gauge R&R.

 - Plan and run lab reliability and qualification campaigns covering thermal, humidity, condensation, solar loading, ingress, cleaning and coating endurance, and field life, then analyze results and drive decisions.

 - Define calibration (intrinsics, extrinsics, per-unit data) and production acceptance tests at our contract manufacturers.

Scale to production and grow the team

 - Take camera systems from concept to volume production with partners and CMs, driving design for manufacturability, automated focus and alignment, and yield.

 - Partner with embedded imaging engineers on sensor bring-up, driver integration and day/night switching in production.

 - Mentor engineers across camera, image quality, test and manufacturing engineering.

 - Track emerging imaging technology (large-format sensors, zoom optics, EO/IR fusion, camera arrays, computational imaging) and recommend where Specter should invest.



Qualifications:

 - 8+ years in optical, imaging or camera systems engineering, with multiple camera products shipped to volume production.

 - Fluency across the stack, from how image quality affects CV/ML and the end user down to lens design, mechanics and test.

 - Deep knowledge of image sensors, lens design and the trade-offs among resolution, FOV, F-number, MTF, aberrations, depth of focus and thermal stability.

 - Hands-on optical simulation with Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or similar.

 - A track record specifying off-the-shelf and custom lenses with suppliers, with clear performance and cost trade-offs.

 - Athermalization experience covering both mechanical design and optical performance across temperature (focus shift, MTF drift).

 - Experience designing optical test equipment and running test campaigns, with rigorous data analysis behind decisions.

 - Experience with NIR imaging and active illumination, as well as L/M/SWIR systems.

 - Experience taking hardware through NPI with contract manufacturers or ODM/JDM partners.

 - Clear communication of optical trade-offs to software, business and customer-facing teams.



Nice to Have

 - Outdoor, automotive or security camera experience, including sealing, condensation, window cleaning and environmental qualification.

 - Active alignment and high-volume camera module manufacturing.

 - PTZ, zoom/focus optics, panoramic or multi-camera systems, and camera calibration for computer vision.

 - EO/IR (thermal) imaging.

 - GMSL/FPD-Link camera interfaces and ISP tuning.

 - Laser illumination and eye-safety certification.

 - Experience leading engineers and cross-functional technical programs.
   

Tool Proficiency

 - Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or equivalent optical design software.

 - Imatest or equivalent image quality analysis tools.

 - Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.

 - Familiarity with MCAD (SolidWorks) for opto-mechanical review.

 - Computer vision fundamentals and tools (OpenCV or similar) for image analysis, calibration and evaluating model performance.

 - Linux command line for sensor bring-up, data capture and scripting on embedded systems.

 - Hardware reliability and test methods: environmental qualification, accelerated life testing, FMEA and failure analysis.

You’ll be responsible for qualifying inbound leads, capturing detailed discovery notes, and guiding prospects through the early stages of the buying journey. You’ll work cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and solutions engineering to help route leads to the right channels and support our mission to bolster U.S. manufacturing automation.



This role is fully remote with the following preferences: NYC metro, North Carolina, California, Illinois, or Texas. 



Responsibilities:

 - Respond promptly and professionally to all inbound sales inquiries from web, email, other channels

 - Qualify inbound leads using pre-defined criteria (e.g. use case Lit, budget, authority, need, timeline)

 - Conduct discovery calls to assess technical feasibility and customer goals

 - Maintain detailed notes in the CRM, including call outcomes, qualification status, and follow-ups

 - Route qualified leads to the appropriate Regional Sales Manager, Applications Engineer , or otherwise

 - Support initial technical Q&A, helping customers understand robot capabilities, system requirements, and deployment Lit

 - Collaborate with marketing to provide feedback on lead quality and messaging gaps

 - Assist in the creation and maintenance of technical sales collateral (e.g., feature sheets, configuration templates, FAQs)

 - Maintain ownership of response time SLAs for lead follow-up

 - Analyze patterns in incoming leads and identify trends or gaps in sales funnel performance

 - Engage in light demo walkthroughs or introductory presentations for early-stage prospects

 - Support lead handoff process into the sales pipeline and help reduce friction in early- stage conversion

title: Account Executive - Bridge
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the Team
The Account Management team at Bridge is dedicated to the growth, retention, and expansion of key customers. Our Scaled Account Management team focuses on driving measurable expansion across a broad portfolio of mid-market and high-growth customers through data-driven strategies, efficient processes, and strong cross-functional partnership.
What You'll Do
As a Scaled Account Manager at Bridge you will own a book of existing accounts and be responsible for expanding revenue, identifying product gaps and driving product adoption, preventing churn and ensuring renewals at scale. You will combine consultative selling with volume playbooks, prioritization based on quantitative signals, and hands-on execution to identify and close upsell opportunities across your territory. As Bridge continues to develop within Stripe’s Money Management organization, you will also drive your customers’ adoption of additional features available through Stripe.
Responsibilities
- Own a book of existing accounts and drive revenue growth through additional usage, upsells, cross-sells, and renewals.
- Develop and execute scalable go-to-market strategies that increase revenue per account and accelerate product adoption across your portfolio.
- Use data and quantitative analysis to prioritize accounts and identify the highest-impact expansion opportunities.
- Generate leads through targeted outreach, research, and campaign execution; manage high-velocity deal cycles from qualification to close.
- Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders to understand business priorities, surface pain points, and tailor Bridge solutions.
- Lead commercial negotiations and renewals to expand and retain customer revenue.
- Identify churn signals in your book and implement strategies to prevent revenue losses.
- Coordinate with product, success, risk, and operations teams to solve complex customer needs and ensure a great user experience.
- Translate customer feedback into actionable product and process improvements to better serve scaled customer segments.
Who You Are
-5–8 years of full sales cycle or account management experience focused on existing business accounts; experience managing a large book of accounts or high-velocity portfolio strongly preferred.
- Strong analytical skills with experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes.
- Comfortable understanding technical product requirements and articulating solutions across multiple technology products.
- Demonstrated ability to close upsell opportunities and manage complex pricing or commercial negotiations.
- Excellent operational acumen and proven ability to manage time and prioritize across a high-volume territory.
- Highly motivated, persistent, and effective in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills.
- Willingness and ability to work in-office in New York or San Francisco at least three days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
- Previous experience at a high-growth payments, fintech, crypto, or technology company.
- Experience with CRM tools, Excel, and basic SQL or a demonstrated comfort with data tools and analysis.
- Background in working cross-functionally with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver outcomes for customers.
Why Bridge
Join a team that values clear thinking, quantitative rigor, and customer obsession. At Bridge you’ll own meaningful customer outcomes, operate with autonomy, and have the opportunity to shape how we scale revenue across high-potential accounts.

description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
In this role, you'd be joining the Alloy Integrations team. We own how Metronome's customers collect payments and recognize revenue. We build and run the integrations that connect Metronome's usage-based billing platform to the systems businesses depend on to get paid: Stripe invoicing and payments, cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud), ERP systems like NetSuite and QuickBooks, and CRM systems like Salesforce. Our team helps Stripe increase the GDP of the internet by making sure every invoice reaches the right system and every payment is collected and accounted for correctly, at scale. We focus on two areas:
Invoicing: collection, dunning, and invoice delivery
Quote-to-cash automation: connecting the full journey from a signed deal to recognized revenue

You'll build and operate distributed systems that move billing data between Metronome and the platforms our customers use to run their finances. The work combines product engineering and reliability. You'll ship features that customers ask for directly, and you'll strengthen the event-driven pipelines that handle large invoicing spikes every month-end.
You'll work closely with our product manager, with partner engineering teams that own contracts, usage rating, and invoice finalization, with solutions architects who build ERP integrations with customers, and with technical support engineers who work with customers every day. Design, build, and maintain integrations between Metronome and external billing, payments, marketplace, ERP, and CRM platforms

title: Director of Product
description:
Via is on a mission to create public transportation systems that provide far greater access to jobs, healthcare, and education. Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and siloed public transportation systems into smart, data-driven, and efficient digital networks. With hundreds of agency partners around the world, Via is recognized as the leading transportation technology and service provider globally.
About the role:
Remix is Via's premier transit planning and scheduling platform, trusted by transit agencies worldwide to design networks, model scenarios, and optimize service. We're looking for a Director of Product to define and drive the next era of Remix: a multimodal planning and scheduling system that gives transit agencies a single, authoritative place to make smarter decisions across every service type they operate.
This is a high-impact, high-ownership role. You will shape the vision for how agencies move from static schedules to data-driven, dynamically optimized operations — balancing labor union rules and contractual constraints with the operational agility modern transit demands. You will own the end-to-end product experience from strategic planning through live execution, and your work will directly affect how millions of riders experience public transit every day.
What you will do:
Define and own the product vision and roadmap for Remix as the global standard for multimodal transit planning and scheduling, spanning fixed route, paratransit, microtransit, and emerging modes
Build the framework for data-driven scheduling — enabling agencies to make optimal use of driver and vehicle time through intelligent analysis of ridership patterns, operational constraints, and service goals
Deeply understand and incorporate labor union rules, collective bargaining agreements, and workforce regulations into the product in a way that is structured yet flexible enough to adapt as those rules evolve
Connect planning and scheduling seamlessly to live operations, reducing the gap between what is scheduled and what is executed — improving accuracy, dispatcher confidence, and rider reliability
Partner closely with engineering, design, data science, and GTM teams to move from vision to shipped product with clear milestones and measurable outcomes
Engage directly and frequently with transit planners, schedulers, and operations leaders to surface unmet needs and validate product direction
Stay current on industry trends, emerging regulations, and competitive dynamics to keep Remix ahead of the market
Who You Are:
You have 10+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex enterprise software products
Have a track record of shipping high-quality products for sophisticated, workflow-heavy enterprise environments where the cost of getting it wrong is high
Are a systems thinker who can hold both strategic vision and operational detail — you know when to zoom out and when to get into the weeds
Have strong instincts for simplifying complexity: translating divergent customer needs and intricate business rules into clean, scalable product decisions
Bring deep empathy for the professionals who use your product daily — planners, schedulers, dispatchers — and design with their real working context in mind
Can quickly become technically fluent in the underlying data models and entities that power scheduling and operations systems — blocks, runs, trips, stops, vehicles, duties, pairings — and can engage at that level of specificity with engineers and architects
Are a strong, credible voice in technical architecture decisions alongside your engineering partners, capable of evaluating tradeoffs and advocating for platform choices that serve both current product needs and long-term scalability
Experience with resource management, labor scheduling, or workforce optimization software is a strong plus
Experience in transportation, transit, or logistics is a plus but not required — intellectual curiosity and the ability to learn technical domains quickly matter more
Compensation and Benefits:
Base salary range: $200,000-$250,000, determined by experience and skills. Total compensation also includes variable pay and equity.
Comprehensive health coverage, with low-cost dental and vision plans.
A 401(k) with a generous company match and vesting.
Fully paid parental leave for new parents, with extended leave options.
Additional benefits (mental health, pet insurance, and other wellness perks).
20 days of paid time off (PTO) annually.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Via is on a mission to create public transportation systems that provide far greater access to jobs, healthcare, and education. Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and siloed public transportation systems into smart, data-driven, and efficient digital networks. With hundreds of agency partners around the world, Via is recognized as the leading transportation technology and service provider globally.
About this role:
Remix is Via's premier transit planning and scheduling platform, trusted by agencies worldwide to design networks, model scenarios, and optimize service. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the Remix platform itself — its usability, scalability, and flexibility — ensuring Remix remains the most powerful and intuitive tool available to transit professionals globally.
This role sits at the center of everything Remix does. You will own the platform foundation that every module is built on, champion AI-led insights that help agencies design better service and measure real performance, and maintain the end-to-end view from planning through operations and back — ensuring data flows in ways that make each step smarter than the last. You are equally comfortable setting long-term platform direction and rolling up your sleeves to sharpen individual features and make each module best in class.
What you'll do:
Own the Remix platform roadmap — usability, scalability, flexibility, and the cross-cutting capabilities that every module depends on
Define and drive the vision for AI-led insights within Remix, enabling transit agencies to make data-informed decisions about service design, network performance, and operational efficiency
Hold the end-to-end product view: from network planning through scheduling and live operations, and back into planning via performance data — ensuring the platform is a continuous feedback loop, not a collection of disconnected tools
Identify and prioritize vertical feature investments across Remix modules, with the rigor to make each one best in class rather than broadly adequate
Partner with engineering and design to raise the bar on platform usability — reducing friction for planners, schedulers, and analysts without sacrificing the depth power users depend on
Work closely with data science and engineering to define how AI and analytics capabilities are surfaced in the product — what insights matter, when they appear, and how they drive action
Engage directly with customers to understand workflow pain points, validate priorities, and pressure-test the roadmap against real operational needs
Stay current on industry trends, competitive products, and emerging technology to ensure Remix leads rather than follows
Who you are:
You have 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of platform or infrastructure-layer products used in complex enterprise workflows
You are a big-picture thinker who can articulate a multi-year platform vision while also making sharp, well-reasoned prioritization calls at the feature level
You have strong instincts for usability and product quality — you notice when something is harder than it needs to be, and you know how to fix it without breaking what works
You understand how AI and data products actually work in practice, and you have experience defining how analytical insights should be integrated into operational workflows in ways users trust and act on
You can quickly become technically fluent in the underlying data models and entities that power planning and scheduling systems, and you are a credible voice in technical architecture decisions alongside your engineering partners — capable of evaluating tradeoffs and advocating for platform choices that serve both current needs and long-term scalability
You have a track record of shipping high-quality features in complex, workflow-heavy enterprise environments where precision and reliability matter
You are collaborative, direct, and effective at building alignment across engineering, design, data science, and go-to-market partners
Experience in transportation, transit, logistics, or resource-intensive industries is a plus; the ability to learn a technical domain quickly is essential
Compensation and Benefits:
Base salary range: $150,000-$200,000, determined by experience and skills. Total compensation also includes variable pay and equity.
Comprehensive health coverage, with low-cost dental and vision plans.
A 401(k) with a generous company match and vesting.

location: United States of America - Texas - Cotulla
description:

Operations Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on
accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where safety, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and teamwork are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Plant Technician
BPX Midstream
ROLE SYNOPSIS:
The Plant Technician is responsible for the safe, environmentally conscious, and economical operation of plant facilities, utilities, and equipment used to produce or refine oil and gas. This role operates plant inlet,
compression, process areas, and associated systems while supporting reliable production, maintenance readiness, process safety, and emergency response.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
• Operate facilities safely, economically, and with environmental awareness.
• Ensure safe working conditions and compliance with all safety and environmental
practices and procedures.
• Develop and execute energy isolation plans for maintenance activities.
• Use the verification application to verify critical work and document failures.
• Operate plant inlet, compression, process areas, and associated systems.
• Maximize production by meeting product specifications, supporting maximum facility runtime, and collaborating effectively with other disciplines and teams.
• Provide positive leadership while contributing as a team player.
• Complete daily read-ups and follow up on parameters outside normal operating ranges.
• Troubleshoot operational and maintenance problems.
• Perform routine housekeeping of the plant and process areas.
• Share knowledge with coworkers and support personal and company business goals and objectives.
• Interface with Maintenance, Production teams, gas distribution companies, and other parts of the BPX organization.
• Identify required maintenance on plant equipment and related systems and
complete computerized work orders.
• Prepare plant equipment and piping systems for maintenance.
• Use available training resources to strengthen technical capabilities.
• Maintain required operator training, emergency preparedness skills, and the
knowledge needed to assist with plant emergencies.
• Use hand tools, climb ladders and stairs to process-vessel elevations, open and close process valves, and operate motor vehicles.
• Take an active role in the Process Safety Management program and DOT pipeline compliance.
ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION:
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• At least five years of experience in oil and gas operations or a related industry.
• Proficiency with mechanical equipment and automation or instrumentation
systems.
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
• Personal commitment to safety and environmental awareness.
• Understanding of process safety concepts and their application.
• Ability to read and use piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) and process flow diagrams (PFDs).
• Willingness and ability to work the assigned 12-hour, 7-on/7-off shift schedule.
• Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, and reporting functions.
• Valid driver's license.
LOCATION & SCHEDULE:
• Location: Hawkville Central CDP
• Schedule: 7 days on / 7 days off, 12-hour shifts
CRITICAL ROLE DEMANDS:
Lifting Abilities
• Lift 72 lbs with two hands from floor to knuckle height twice, with 12-second rest intervals between lifts.
• Lift 72 lbs with two hands from floor to waist height twice, with 12-second rest intervals between lifts.
• Lift 60 lbs with two hands from floor to shoulder height twice, with 12-second rest intervals between lifts.
• Lift 30 lbs with two hands from floor to crown height twice, with 12-second rest intervals between lifts.
Pushing & Pulling Abilities:
• Push horizontally with both hands positioned between waist and mid-chest height to generate a peak force of 120 lbs, three times.
• Pull horizontally with both hands positioned between waist and mid-chest height to generate a peak force of 120 lbs, three times.
Carrying Abilities
• Carry 72 lbs with two hands at a self-selected height for 10 feet, twice, at a self selected pace.
• Carry at least 50 lbs with one hand for a minimum distance of 50 feet.
Stair and Ladder Climbing Abilities
• Climb up and down a total of 40 steps at a self-selected pace.
• Climb up and down 14 ladder rungs at a self-selected pace.
Agilities
• Stooping and twisting: From standing, perform three continuous alternate toe
touches to each side at a self-selected pace. Reach toward the toes on the
opposite side as far as possible; touching the toes is not required.
• Kneeling: From standing, kneel on one knee, return to full standing, and kneel on the opposite knee. Repeat three times on each knee at a self-selected but continuous pace.
• Sustained squatting: From standing, lower into a functional squat, hold the position for 30 seconds, and return to standing.
• Repetitive squatting: Perform three squats at a self-selected pace with no hold at the end range.
